note: This file is the sole canonical owner of every version and versioning-policy value in this repository. package.json#version, CHANGELOG.md, the README versioning section and docs/versioning-policy.md are projections of it and are never read back as a source.

conceptualMapping.note: The conceptual milestone maps to package version 0.1.0 and never to 1.0.0. SemVer rule 5 makes 1.0.0 a definition of a public API, and no decision has authorized one. The mapping is a plan, not a permission: reaching 0.1.0 is itself a human completion decision.

ceiling.note: No current value and no recommendation may rank above 0.1.0. The ceiling moves only when a human writes a decision record here whose newCeiling agrees with maxVersion. This is a review tripwire, not a cryptographic gate.

currentVersion.note: 0.0.0-planning is syntactically valid SemVer and was always a pre-release of a version that was never released. It is preserved as a historical planning placeholder and is never used going forward. Moving to 0.1.0-alpha.1 is a pointer move on an unpublished private package identity: it publishes nothing, tags nothing and produces no artifact.

unreleasedProvenance.role: the fail-closed governance and boundary verification surface
this canonical versioning and changelog policy

authorityBinding.note: This package moves no dimension of the authority in force. It records the binding so that a version decision can never be taken against a stronger authority than the one that exists.

parity.note: A parity finding always names the projection that moved. Editing this file until it agrees with a projection turns a copy into a source and is never the repair.

nonGoals: any release, cut, tag, GitHub Release, npm publish, deployment or production step
any movement of kernelReady, sdkReady, appBuildable, releaseAllowed, deployAllowed, productionAllowed or gapClosed
any claim of completeness, MVP or a finished kernel
changelog automation derived from a git log
any edit to repository-status.json, planning, db, src or the five pre-existing checkers
any Git operation by the writer: commit, push, branch, merge, rebase or tag
raising the ceiling, which is a human decision and not an outcome of running anything
